Daily Digest Wednesday, September 9, 2026

68% of Marketers Are "Disconnected" in AI Strategy, Google + Accenture Launch FDE Unit, Dark Data Wrecks AI Stacks

Adobe: 68% of marketers disconnected from AI strategy. Google races to catch up with Accenture FDE deal. Dark data quietly wrecking AI marketing stacks.

  1. 1

    Adobe Study: 68% of Marketers Are "Disconnected" in AI Strategy

    A new Adobe Business study categorizes enterprise marketers on their AI maturity and finds the vast majority operating AI in silos — disconnected from repeatable systems and shared governance. The CX AI Maturity Index shows 68.3% fall into the "Disconnected" category, meaning AI exists but only in isolated instances. Just 15.3% are "Orchestrated" with connected, controlled experiences. The insight: 64% can't trace how their AI-driven content was generated, and 74% describe customer journeys as siloed or partially coordinated.

  2. 2

    Google Cloud + Accenture Launch FDE Unit for Enterprise AI Deployment

    Google Cloud and Accenture are forming the "Accenture Gemini Enterprise Business Group" — a joint unit deploying forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) directly into enterprises to help them adopt Google's AI tools. Google will train up to 1,000 FDEs as it races to catch up with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Microsoft in the implementation wars. Per Ramp data, Google accounts for just 6% of enterprise AI spending vs. Anthropic's 43.5% and OpenAI's 39.7%. The new bet: implementation can become its own trillion-dollar business.

    Read on TechCrunch ↗
  3. 3

    Voicing AI Ships "Knowledge Mesh" — A Context Layer for AI Agents

    Voicing AI launched Knowledge Mesh, an enterprise knowledge layer designed to solve the context problem that's killing AI projects. Gartner predicts 40%+ of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by 2027 due to escalating costs and unclear value — and the diagnosis is context failure, not model failure. The market for "AI context platforms" — software that governs and delivers organized knowledge to agents — is sized at $28B in 2026, growing to $78B by 2030. The insight: organizations that prioritize semantics can improve agentic AI accuracy by 80% and cut costs by 60%.

  4. 4

    Dark Data Is Quietly Wrecking AI Marketing Stacks

    Roughly 90% of enterprise data is unstructured, and most marketing orgs have no idea how much is poisoning their AI models. The culprits: creator bios in five formats, campaign briefs buried in PDFs, contract terms scattered across emails. Dark data problems rarely cause dramatic failures — they cause slow, silent degradation. Only 21% of CRM data is structured enough for AI creator matching. The pattern: AI compliance checkers flag problems days after posts go live, not before.

  5. 5

    Klaviyo Pushes Into Enterprise, AI Agents, and International

    At the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference, Klaviyo outlined an aggressive expansion into enterprise software, AI agents, and international markets. The email/SMS marketing platform is betting that predictive AI and autonomous agents can differentiate it from traditional marketing automation incumbents. With 70+ automation templates and AI-powered behavioral prediction, it's a signal that even mid-market martech players see agentic AI as table stakes. Read this one: The Adobe study on marketers being "disconnected" is a gut-check moment. 68% operating AI in silos with no shared governance. 64% can't trace how their content was generated. This isn't an AI capability problem — it's an organizational design problem wearing AI's clothes. PMM leaders who can build the connective tissue between AI tools and actual workflows have the advantage.
